summary: The male rat worksheet of Table S2 supplies 27-versus-6-month log2 fold changes and adjusted P values for 817 selected whole-hypothalamus genes. The analyses paired 613/817 (75.03%) genes, with 604/612 nonzero pairs agreeing in direction. Incomplete reference coverage and the author's exclusion of one registered aged animal limit concordance.

manualReview.summary: Published 27-versus-6-month effects compared for selected hypothalamus genes
manualReview.note: The male rat worksheet of Table S2 supplies 27-versus-6-month log2 fold changes and adjusted P values for 817 selected whole-hypothalamus genes. The authors selected genes across later ages versus 6 months using a 1.5-fold change and BH-adjusted P below 0.05. The deposited code applies FC > 1.5 or FC < 1/1.5. All listed hypothalamus rows contribute regardless of their 27-month significance or trajectory class. Both studies compare independent male Sprague-Dawley rat hypothalami from the same collection. All 12 young animals and 11 aged animals are shared. Explorer uses all 12 aged animals, including Age27m_11 (GSM9417680, RNA ID 1553267), which Table S1 excludes after isotree outlier detection, low RNA quality and low mapping rate. The author model also uses the intermediate-age libraries for normalization and variance estimation. Effects could be paired for 613/817 (75.03%) selected genes. Both numerical agreement routes pass on paired effects. Reference coverage falls below the 90% requirement, and one endpoint animal differs. Pearson 0.9325, Spearman 0.9264 and 604/612 same-direction nonzero pairs (98.69%). The deposited count checksum is confirmed. The full audit is in data/author-validation/continued-sources/GSE314970/codex-2026-11-24/SEARCH_LOG.md.

comparabilityReview.basis: Registered edgeR quasi-likelihood GLM with TMM on unrounded ArrayStudio counts, an intercept and groupcase. Each coefficient is the 27-month group minus its 6-month baseline.
comparabilityReview.reference: Shavlakadze et al., Science Advances, DOI 10.1126/sciadv.ady8401, Supplementary Table S2, male rat, tissue = hypothalamus. The authors selected genes across later ages versus 6 months using a 1.5-fold change and BH-adjusted P below 0.05. The deposited code applies FC > 1.5 or FC < 1/1.5. All listed hypothalamus rows contribute regardless of their 27-month significance or trajectory class.

cohort.note: Both studies compare independent male Sprague-Dawley rat hypothalami from the same collection. All 12 young animals and 11 aged animals are shared. Explorer uses all 12 aged animals, including Age27m_11 (GSM9417680, RNA ID 1553267), which Table S1 excludes after isotree outlier detection, low RNA quality and low mapping rate. The author model also uses the intermediate-age libraries for normalization and variance estimation.

contrast.note: Both coefficients compare 27-month males against 6-month males within whole rat hypothalamus. The endpoint coefficient is distinct from each trajectory slope and every other age contrast.

features.note: Both pipelines sum duplicate source GeneName labels. Applying the pinned release-113 mRatBN7.2 annotation to those groups recovers Cd4, Spaar and LOC100910620. The registered Or12d14 and Krt18 features each combine distinct author labels and remain unpaired. Each paired registered feature corresponds to exactly one author GeneName group. Unpaired rows comprise 116 named features without a published coefficient, 86 features without a public symbol, 2 features combining distinct author labels.

effects.note: Both report old-minus-young log2 fold change. Author values are rounded to two decimals. Pearson 0.9325, Spearman 0.9264 and 604/612 same-direction nonzero pairs (98.69%). Median absolute difference 0.0700 log2 units. Registered/author RMS effect ratio 1.0211.

inference.note: Table S2 prints adjusted P values to three decimals. On 613 finite pairs, 379 author and 303 registered values are below 0.05, with 296 in both. Across the complete selected reference and the complete registered output the counts are 483 and 941. 2 paired author values print as 0.050, leaving their unrounded classification unknown. The endpoint raw author P values are unavailable. The authors' original selection also used a fold-change cutoff. These descriptive counts use adjusted P alone.

coverage.note: 613/817 (75.03%) selected author rows paired to 15,373 published registered genes. Every row of the tissue-specific author list contributes to the denominator. Unpaired genes are unassessed.

comparabilityReview.criteria: For a selected reference, author-concordance-v2 requires at least 30 pairs and 90% reference coverage, compatible cohort, contrast, identifiers and effect definitions, and either Pearson and Spearman each at least 0.90 or at least 90% directional agreement over at least 30 nonzero pairs spanning at least 90% of all pairs. Magnitude and inference are contextual.
comparabilityReview.conclusion: Effects could be paired for 613/817 (75.03%) selected genes. Both numerical agreement routes pass on paired effects. Reference coverage falls below the 90% requirement, and one endpoint animal differs.
